utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from that location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you saw uniforms -- or rather, were you able to observe the uniforms that the Serb soldiers wore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the same kind of uniforms that you used to see on Serb soldiers for whom you said you could observe with the naked eye or through binoculars? Were they wearing the same uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing the same uniforms, but this was a relatively bad image, more black and white, so I couldn't distinguish the colours. But the uniforms seemed similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will show you another document. This is a Drina Corps document, the title being "analysis of the conduct of combat operations in the operation code named Pesnica, Fist," being the English translation. The number of the document is 04342072.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we move on to this other document I would just like to inquire whether since the witness did not necessarily testify to what we heard on the screen, if we're having a technical problem, that we resolve this issue as to whether the transcript is an accurate reflection of what was said. And then the other thing I would just like to raise in the transcript, Your Honour, is that I believe that sometimes we have a description of the first soldier, we have 60-millimetre shell, and I do not understand the language, but certainly do not think that it was what was said was preceded by a description of what it was. Maybe the first man --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. I had thought about that myself when I received the two pages, the transcript. That's not something that the accused [sic] had. The accused was following the video recording. The transcript is for us. The transcript is for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: But, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In his testimony he did identify --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You mean the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. In his testimony he did identify the weapon. He referred to it by its calibre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I had this same idea as yours when I saw the transcript because for a moment I thought: Is this a suggestion that is being put to the witness to say that this is a 60-millimetre -- 60-millimetre shell. So it's -- but I don't think there is any problem there because I don't think he had these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. And I just wonder if this is going to be entered into evidence, the transcript as is, or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. The evidence as -- what is entered -- is entered already in the evidence is your P317.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I don't know if it has a transcript or not. I obviously don't expect you to remember from so many months ago. It has one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Not necessarily this section, but yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I obviously haven't checked the transcript of that part of the video from your side. If it doesn't tally with what is here, please draw our attention, and I mean we will give it all our -- due attention. However, I wouldn't worry about the 60-millimetre calibre issue because what he understands -- what he had in front of him was the video recording and not -- all right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move. Does that cover everything that you raised or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I believe it does. Once the transcript will not be placed into evidence, then I think the problem is resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right -- no, the transcript is in evidence. It has been tendered and I have given it a number. The transcript has been -- this is why I told you that if you think that this transcript does not reflect the words that were being uttered by the various persons on screen or if it doesn't tally or correspond with the translation that you might have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If they are contesting the correctness, the faithfulness of the reproduction of those words in the transcript, then please do tell us so. We are not in a position to confirm that its a faithful presentation of what was said or not because as you suggested we could barely hear the words that were being said, which were being said in Serbo-Croat in any case. And to my knowledge, from what I was following at the time, the -- the interpreters in the English booth also at some point in time couldn't follow. So it is being admitted into evidence, obviously, but if the correctness of the presentation is being challenged by you, then obviously that will be taken into consideration. But for the time being, this is what we have.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you a document entitled "analysis of the conduct of combat operations in the operation code named Pesnica, Fist," number 04342072. I will draw your attention to parts of the document starting from paragraph 2 which says: "Operation Pesnica was conducted pursuant -- from the 11th of January, 1993 to 20th January, 1993." Please look at the last paragraph on this page which says: "The primary task of the units in conducting operation Pesnica was to cut the Muslim forces' area of concentration and to separate the Srebrenica area from Cerska area and liberate the Milici-Konjevic Polje-Zvornik road, prevent Muslim penetration into Bratunac by powerful Defence, and break up enemy forces along the Bratunac-Kravica-Konjevic Polje axes by active operations." My question to you is as follows: Does this document reflect the actual situation in the Podrinje area as far as you know in January 1993, especially with regard to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These Serb attacks in the time period mentioned under this combat operation's analysis cause great harm to the civilian population in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely, very much so, especially by shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of them were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In hundreds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the events surrounding the fall of Konjevic Polje? How did the Serb military treat civilians when Konjevic Polje fell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall it was right before Konjevic Polje fell. I have to point out that I wasn't there. It was where there was UN presence in Hrncici, to be precise, near a mosque there. There was a large group of people gathered there and a UN vehicle. From what I heard from my neighbour, the UN vehicle and all the civilians gathered around it were directly targeted. On that occasion, dozens of civilians were killed. This man told me that he was able to see with his own eyes a shell hitting directly a UN soldier holding a child in his arms. He was killed on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the civilians were withdrawing from Konjevic Polje towards Srebrenica, were civilian columns directly targeted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was retreating towards Srebrenica, I happened to be in Pervani, which is part of Urkovici. I set out toward Srebrenica, and between Sandici and Lolici, in the direction of Rogac, three tanks were positioned there. I haven't mentioned these tanks before, but they were constantly there on a hill overlooking our area. And they were constantly - and I mean the tanks - opening fire on the civilians passing there. As I was passing through that stretch of the road, I experienced terrifying scenes, civilians getting killed. I came across a woman who is a close relative of mine. She received a direct hit from a tank and was killed. She was pregnant and her child was thrown out of her womb by the impact. In addition to the civilians who, as they were heading towards Srebrenica, took their cattle with them, cattle was also killed in large numbers. And I can tell you that the cattle suffered as much as people did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Ms. Vidovic. Let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait -- yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whatever the situation, you managed to reach Srebrenica. But now I wish to go back to another issue to save time, and we'll ask you something concerning the organisation of defence in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we haven't given this document a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document, which consists of two pages in B/C/S and two pages being the translation thereof into English with the ERN 04342072 to 073 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D942.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, as far as the defence of Konjevic Polje is concerned, you repeatedly mentioned groups in your testimony. In the course of 1992 in the area of Konjevic Polje through to the fall of Konjevic Polje, did you have an organised brigade in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already indicated, from the start until Konjevic Polje fell, there were only groups that were active there except for Nurif Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the group -- did the people join these groups on a voluntary basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. They joined them of their own free will because they were defending their families and homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they able to switch from one group to another whenever they wanted to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were able to do so. Whoever wanted to switch over to different group, he was able to do so without any difficulties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the usher's assistance now in showing the witness D649. While the document is being distributed, I will say for the record that this is a document by the Municipal Staff, defence staff of Bratunac, dated 29 November 1992. Establishment -- reformation of units of the armed forces of the Army of the Republic of BiH -- of BH in Bratunac municipality. And I quote: "Pursuant to the decision on the organisation of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, order of the Main Staff of the OS BiH, order of the Tuzla district defence staff, strictly confidential, number 03/46, and the order of the Tuzla OK SO, strictly confidential, number 03/174, we demand the following organisational changes: "1) form: "(a) form a 114th Eastern Bosnian Brigade number T-411.024. "(b) form battalion I, II, III, IV, V number T-411.024." Witness, first of all, do you see the date in the upper left corner, 29 November 1992, and then to the -- on the right-hand side there's a stamp saying 19 December 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the incoming mail stamp containing date 19 December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of 1992 in Konjevic Polje in your own native village, I don't want to mention its name, did you hear of the establishment of the 114th Eastern Bosnian Brigade in Konjevic Polje? Did that actually happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of that. But this could never really take hold in the Konjevic Polje area because you see from this document there's the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th Battalion. Well, you didn't have people to fill up one battalion, let alone five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that according to this document the request for the establishment of the brigade was drafted only on the 29th November, 1992 -- or rather, as early as 29 November, and was received by the municipal staff only on the 19th December 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already touched upon this matter but I want to ask you further. According to what you knew about the situation in Konjevic Polje, were there any conditions in place for the establishment of a brigade? Were -- was there equipment enough? Were there enough human resources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no conditions in place in Konjevic Polje for such an establishment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could I show the witness another document, please? This is Prosecution Exhibit P94, sequel from the continuations to the guide number 69/94. Look at 142888. In the English version, Your Honours, that's at page 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, look under Roman numeral VI, full establishment title of the unit 284th East Bosnian Light Brigade, headquartered in Srebrenica. At the bottom it says: "Since their establishment until the 21st January 1994," and there it says: "114th East Bosnian Light Brigade," and then look at next page. But however, I want to ask you first: How would you comment on this document which says that there was the 284th Brigade in Srebrenica? What was this all about? Can you tell the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that there is no 114th but rather 284th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are now in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I wish to draw your attention to a portion of this document on the following page. We said that on this earlier page there was 114th East Bosnian Brigade and then the next page relates the events related to this brigade. Let's look at the part where it says: "On the 27th of" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Madam Vidovic repeat her quote because the interpreter didn't manage to catch it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, we have a problem, because the interpreters didn't catch up the last part of your statement. If you could repeat it -- in fact, you are being asked to be kind enough to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise. 114th Eastern Bosnian Brigade and then different events are related. And then it says: "On the 27th of April, 1992, the ultimatum for the surrendering of weapon to the local commune of Konjevic Polje issued by the Chetniks from Bratunac is being rejected -- or was rejected."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can we claim in any sense that at this given time, at the time the ultimatum was issued to Konjevic Polje, the 114th Brigade was in existence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One could not say that the 114th Brigade was in existence in any sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have finished with this document. Please take a look at another document, another Prosecution exhibit, P93. I believe this is a sequel or a continuation of the other document. I will quote the -- from the top of this page. It says: "114th Eastern Bosnian Brigade, 1st Cerani Detachment, 6th Detachment Kamenica, and 16th Muslim Brigade participated in the protection of the return of civilians on the location Perunike and caused great losses in manpower and technique on the enemy. On the 26th of September, 1992, in coordination with the 1st CO, Rogosija was temporarily liberated." Based on your knowledge, on the 26th of September, 1992, was there a 114th Brigade in existence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 114th Brigade never existed from the start up until Konjevic Polje fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with this I want to ask you the following. As far as you know, did anybody from your area participate in these clashes at Kamenica and Rogosija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, these -- the distance between these places and Konjevic Polje is some ten kilometres, and we were unable to provide any assistance to them. We were weak enough as -- on our own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I believe we have finished with this document. We wish to save time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to show a brief video-clip to the witness which has to do with the events surrounding the fall of Srebrenica in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, before that I wish to ask you the following, Witness. Do you remember where you were on the 12th of July, 1995? Was your father ill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My father, who was not of an advanced age that much, but he was quite ill at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember your whereabouts on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that date, early in the morning, I headed out of Srebrenica. I started from the Srebrenica stadium and reached Potocari at about 1100 or 1200 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your father with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the scene that you saw as you reached the UN base at Potocari? Could you explain it for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first priority was to find transportation for my mother and father, to have them transported to Tuzla. I went, therefore, directly to the spot where vehicles that were supposed to head up for Tuzla were parked -- were supposed to be parked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice the conduct of the Serb police officers and soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Close by there were Serb soldiers and Serb policemen, although the policemen were closer to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Yes, Ms. Sellers, is it about relevance?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, one certainly could raise the issue of relevance. The Defence has brought similar brief questions about this time period up before, but here I think that we do have in one of the questions: Did you notice the conduct of the Serb police officers. The Prosecution is not doubting who could be present, but if the witness is going to speak about this section of his testimony, I think that he can do it quite willingly and without having a leading question. The relevance, we will keep a close eye on it as it relates to this indictment. That would be our main concern here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And if I may ask at this point what's the relevance of these events to the indictment, which goes back to 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It goes to the credibility of some of the OTP witnesses, and I will move very fast through it, Your Honour. It has to do with the credibility of some of the Prosecutor's witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll wait and see. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about Serb soldiers and policemen. Can you tell me whether you recognised your neighbours from Kravica amongst them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Right away I recognised Nikola Popovic, who was moving in my vicinity who was son of Kostadin from Kravica -- actually, I knew Kostadin very well because he is two or three years older than me. His son, though, is much younger, but I knew him pretty well as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this in the vicinity of your father and some other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He stood close to two people that I will point to at -- in this video-clip that I recognised.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like the video-clip to be shown now. The video should begin at 19.38 until 20.06.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic's microphone was not on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is Nikola Kostadinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Nikola Popovic, son of Kostadin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was an omission in the transcript; now it has been corrected. Is that the person that you saw that day across from the base in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the person carrying the machine-gun. I know that weapon very well, and I used to have one when I served my time and when I served my military term in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please continue at 21.24.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is another person next to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now the witness said that this is another person. Could we enter that into the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First I think we need to go back to the previous point, I think it was 20.10, when he pointed out -- at someone. And now we are at -- if we could go back and do all this properly. Can you start from there, 19.51, please, because he stopped while it was still running -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, please, and go back, this small portion, because when we were being shown those soldiers, he did make some comments, he did say something, and he was sort of suggesting that we stop so that he could tell us something. So let's start from there first, please. No, it's not this one, it's 20.10, in that region. 25 -- yes, you can play from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Keep on going, keep on going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah, here, this is where we are starting. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. Stop. Now, when you saw this gentleman on the screen, you wanted to say something or you said something, but I never got it. Could you explain what you were saying here at 20.28, if I am seeing right. It looks like 20.28. Who is the gentleman with --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Nikola Popovic, son of Kostadin Popovic. I used to know Kostadin Popovic very well. He was my senior by two or three years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is when the witness said that this was no longer the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. This is what I want to hear from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was something else I wanted you to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the last person we saw with something resembling a Zolja on his back, is that Kostadin Popovic or not, the last person you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Kostadin but Nikola.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, Nikola.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is no longer Nikola. Nikola was there before. He had a T-shirt with a light machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you know who this last person that we saw, if you could go back with the video a few clips. This is the soldier with the head-scarf and Zolja on his back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This soldier with the head-scarf and a Zolja on his back, who then turns on -- towards the children and women on the other side and tells them, Don't be afraid, do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't recognise him. He was -- he came from the other side. Popovic came from below where the group was, and this man came from the other side. So I couldn't see him directly or I couldn't see his face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is from the village of Lolici. I don't know his name, but I know his father's name, Bajro Omerovic. I know him quite well, but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please continue with the recording.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Ramiz Mujcinovic, aka Bugar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And for the record, this is at 22.03. The previous one I missed the exact time of it, if you have it Ms. Vidovic, or we could go back. The other gentleman from Lolici whose name he doesn't know but whose father's name he knows, what was the precise moment --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At 21.51, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you knew this person. Where is he from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's from Hrncici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, where did your father stay at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was with him then and we were very close to these people that we saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would just like to know are we still in the realm of credibility of witness or identification, or are we in a different realm?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Quite a pertinent question, actually. Where are we now? Because, okay, I can understand the previous part relating to Nikola Popovic, but what's this part about now, for relevance purposes more than anything else?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is also about Nikola Popovic and some other witnesses, as you will realise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go ahead and see. Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you about your father. Where did he remain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we noticed that men are being separated from women and being taken aside, my father pushed me away and he said, Run away from here. I'll remain, whatever may happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see? Who separated men from women and who was close to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs were separating men from women, and Serb police in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a specific person in mind. Did you notice anyone specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could see, Popovic, Nikola, was one of the most dangerous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him take away some men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These men had already been separated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber what the fate was of the two men you identified and that of your father. Have they ever returned alive or resurfaced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 12th of July, 1995, in Potocari up until today, I don't know about the fate of either my father or the remaining two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If one were to say that Nikola Popovic played soccer in Milici on that day, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct that he wasn't at that place on the 12th of July, 1995, based on what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, 1995, when men were being separated from the women next to the base in Potocari, was he there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he was. I knew him well and I wouldn't dare say he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the fall of Srebrenica, did you ever speak with some people to try and establish what the fate of your father was? Did you talk to the other people who were there in Potocari and in Kravica, trying to find out what happened with your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the columns passed by, there were some trucks, some with tarpaulin on, some without it. And when they passed through Kravica, the women who knew Nikola Popovic, he -- they said that he was right there at the spot next to the so-called Oka where over 1.000 Muslims were executed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To ask you something else. You have already explained about Nikola Popovic, but did you discuss other people from Kravica and their participation when it comes to Oka, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought you were asking me specifically about Nikola Popovic, but as regards other people from Kravica, they participated in it. Because all of the women said that these people were predominantly from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we put another document before the witness. I believe it to be the last for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But before we do that, we have never had -- I mean, I've gone through the transcript. There's no reference to this video that we have last seen and it is not yet in evidence. So -- on the paper that you distributed before you started the examination-in-chief, there is a reference, obviously; there is V0004417. But in the transcript there is no reference to this video, so we need to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I apologise, Your Honour. This is a video, V0004417, two of two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And is it --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received it from the OTP according to the receipt number 153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And you are tendering it in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So this will -- this video will become Defence Exhibit D943, 943. We are already four or five minutes past the half-hour. How many more minutes do you think you require to finish your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then we have the break and then we start with the cross-examination afterwards. But then if we go ten more minutes -- if it's okay with everyone, we go ten more minutes. The interpreters and the technicians, do you prefer to go ten more minutes now or break now and continue in half an hour's time? It's not going to change anything because we will have very little time for Ms. Sellers to -- for her cross-examination. Let's have a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we give the last document to the witness, please. This is a document bearing the number of 04632267, a document by the government of Republika Srpska, delivery note on the amendment to the report with attachments, dated the 30th of March, 2005, from the working group for implementation of conclusions from the final report made by the commission for investigation of events in and around Srebrenica and the period from the 10th to the 19th July, 1995. Your Honours, on the next page we find but a relevant portion of the report being a very voluminous one. I just wanted you to see the page 04632283. I quote: "The working group found that 17.342 persons participated in the events in and around Srebrenica in the 10th until the 19th July 1995, and that the working group fully identifies 17.074 persons, participants of the subject events in attachment number 6." Your Honours, we made an excerpt from the attachment with the relevant pages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at page 3. It says: "Annex 6: Identified participants." Do you agree with me? Could you speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go to the next page. I wanted to ask you about some of the people and whether you knew them, and perhaps you can offer a comment if necessary. Number 3537 Veseljko Bogicevic, son of Vojislav, Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, 3537. Starting from the top, and from the beginning this is page 4. Were you able to find it? Veseljko Bogicevic, son of Vojislav. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3537, I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please turn the next page. 3768. Dragan Djuric, son of Cedo, do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Turn another page, please, number 3810, Slavisa Eric, son of Kosan. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him. He was the nurse we mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony you said you mention -- you spoke with many people about the events in Srebrenica. Did you hear anything of Slavisa Eric's presence in the area of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since he was a noticeable person and a nurse as well, women know him better than men, hence I know some things about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn from those people whether Slavisa Eric was in the area of Kravica around the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the women said so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If one were to claim that Eric at that time was absent from the area of Srebrenica, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please turn another page, number 4695, Ratko Nikolic, son of Paja. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really, not directly in any case. But they come from the area of Kravica, or to be more precise from Kajici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn anything about his participation in the events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard what the women who knew him could tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Turn another page, number 4865, Nikola Petrovic, son of Milos. Do you know this person and did you hear anything of -- about his participation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you heard nothing of his participation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To return to the previous question, Your Honours, when we discussed Ratko Nikolic, it is unclear from the transcript. The witness stated it rather clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear and from whom regarding Ratko Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards Ratko Nikolic, I heard that he was a close relative of Nikolic, Jovan's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about his presence in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The women said they saw him in Kravica when the Muslim population was gathered at Oka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you heard nothing about Nikola Petrovic, son of Milos. At the bottom, number 4904, Nikola Popovic, son of Kostadin, is that the person you mentioned in your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 4904, the same page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see the first and last names. Is that the person you testified about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turn the next page of the report. Number 5005, Slavoljub Rankic, son of Nedjo. Did you hear anything about that person and do you know him? Did you hear anything pertaining to 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 5014, further down below, Milo Rankovic, son of Vaso. Did you hear anything about that person and do you know him, 5014?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next page, please. Number 5195, Milenko Stevanovic, son of Radivoje. Do you know this person and did you hear anything about his as regards the events in 1995? ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the next page, 15.848, Stanisa Stevanovic, son of Dragoljub. Did you ever hear about this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 15.848. Do you know this person and did you hear anything as to his participation in the events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment on this person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we assign an exhibit number to this part of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So this document is going to be described first. It consists of the following pages: A page in Serbo-Croat, with ERN 04632266, and this is a delivery note of the Republika Srpska government report mentioned by Madam Vidovic and with -- in it a receipt by a representative of the Tribunal, Prosecution, signed on the 6th of October -- well, on the signature it seems to be 6th of October, but in the translation it is 4th of October. So anyway it's -- on the original it's signed on the 6th of October, 2005. This is accompanied by an establish translation thereof with ERN number 04632267. Then in the Serbo-Croat language there is a photocopy of page 15 of the report with ERN 04632283. This is accompanied by a partial translation of that page or a translation of part of that page into English. The English version carries the same ERN number. Then there are nine pages in B/C/S being extracts of names from the annex mentioned by Madam Vidovic. They run from number 1 till 15.887, not in a properly sequential order, and they seem to be extracted from an annex or document which has the number 319. This part of the exhibit is accompanied by a page in the English language which translates only the heading and subheadings of the relevant parts of Annex 6. Then finally there is a page in English containing abbreviations, or more than abbreviations, a translation into English of the various terms, rank -- designating ranks from Serbo-Croat into English. All this is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D943 -- 944? Oh, yeah, that was the video. Yes. This is 944. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, just one matter. In describing this document you're referring to numbers which don't appear to be in sequential order. In my understanding that's referring to the identity, the numbers are, but there's a proper sequence from 1 to 15.877. There's nothing improper in that sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All I'm saying is that you skip, for example, from page 69 to page 73, from page 74 to page 90, from page 90 to page 93, from page 93 to 95, 95 to 99, and from 99 to page 297 basically. Thank you for observing that. I think it's clear for everyone. Yes, any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. Ms. Sellers, you've got 22 minutes, and I suggest that you start so that we'll make a humongous effort afterward try to finish with your cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will start today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Cross-examined by Ms. Sellers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I will be asking you questions on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor, and my duties are to try and elicit evidence from you to clarify some of the evidence that you've given and to allow you to explain, not only to the Trial Chamber, to the public, very important factual matters in this case. Since we are in the situation where your identity has been protected by the Trial Chamber, I would ask you to assist me. If I ask you a question and you understand in your answer that you might reveal some identifying information, please stop and ask prior to answering that question to go into private session. I, on my part, will try and be conscious with the questions and the way I form them as to the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So therefore, I would like to start by asking the Trial Chamber, could we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've testified, as many men from the former Yugoslavia, that you spent time in the JNA as part of your official duties of citizenhood. Is that correct? You will have to speak into the microphone. I switch mine off, but you can't just nod. You have to now say something.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I served the regular military service in the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified that among the things that you did for your military service was work as a border guard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Before that I had training in Skofja Loka.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that the time is up now and I imagine that we should stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you so much, Ms. Sellers and Ms. Vidovic. We will stop here for today, sir, and we will proceed with your cross-examination tomorrow, hoping that we will finish by tomorrow so that on Monday we can start with a new witness. May I just remind you what I told you on each and every day that you've been here, that between now and tomorrow you've not to communicate with anyone on the subject matter of your testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
